hints: Differentiate $x = \tan^2(2t)$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule to obtain $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 4\tan(2t)\sec^2(2t)$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $x = (\tan(2t))^2$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2\tan(2t) \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}[\tan(2t)] = 2\tan(2t) \cdot (2\sec^2(2t)) = 4\tan(2t)\sec^2(2t)$$

Express $\tan(2t)$ and $\sec^2(2t)$ in terms of $\sin(2t)$ and $\cos(2t)$:
$$\tan(2t)\sec^2(2t) = \dfrac{\sin(2t)}{\cos(2t)} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\cos^2(2t)} = \dfrac{\sin(2t)}{\cos^3(2t)}$$

Substitute back into the derivative fraction:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{-2\sin(2t)}{4\left(\dfrac{\sin(2t)}{\cos^3(2t)}\right)} = -\dfrac{2\sin(2t)}{4\sin(2t)} \cdot \cos^3(2t) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^3(2t)$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Parametric Curves: Differentiates $x$ using chain rule to get $4\tan 2t \sec^2 2t$ (M1A1). Differentiates $y$ to get $-2\sin 2t$ (B1). Uses $dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt)$ to obtain $-\frac{1}{2}\cos^3 2t$ (B1).

hints: Find the point coordinates $(x, y)$ and tangent gradient at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$.
Find the normal gradient $m = -\dfrac{1}{m_{\text{tangent}}}$ and write the line equation in the form $y = mx + c$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gradient of the tangent at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^3 = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{8}\right) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{8}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal, $m = -\dfrac{1}{m_{\text{tangent}}}$:
$$m = -\dfrac{1}{-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{8}} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{2} = 4\sqrt{2}$$

Write the equation of the normal passing through $\left(1, \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$:
$$y - \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 4\sqrt{2}(x - 1)$$

Expand and rearrange into the form $y = mx + c$:
$$y = 4\sqrt{2}x - 4\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$
Combine the constant terms:
$$-4\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = -\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = -\dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}$$
$$y = 4\sqrt{2}x - \dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Equations of Normals: Evaluates $x = 1, y = \sqrt{2}/2$ (B1). Finds normal gradient $4\sqrt{2}$ from tangent gradient $-\sqrt{2}/8$ (B1). Sets up normal equation (M1). Obtains three-term form $y = 4\sqrt{2}x - \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}$ (A1).
